title: Public Database Exposure: Production PostgreSQL on Port 5432
business_impact: Your customer database appears to be directly accessible from the public internet. If an attacker connects, customer names, passwords, and order records could be stolen or held for ransom.
technical_explanation: AWS RDS instance 'production-postgres-01' has PubliclyAccessible=True and security group ingress allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 5432.
potential_consequence: Catastrophic data breach, total customer database exfiltration, GDPR regulatory fines.
recommended_action: Remove public access and restrict database connections exclusively to your application private subnet.
remediation_steps: ["Open AWS RDS Console -> Databases -> production-postgres-01 -> Modify", "Under Connectivity, toggle 'Public access' to 'No'", "Set Security Group inbound rules to allow TCP 5432 only from sg-ecommerce-api", "Verify database connection string inside ecommerce-api container"]

title: Dormant Administrator Account: Dev Ops Admin (Contractor)
business_impact: A contractor account with full administrative AWS rights has not been used for 142 days and has no two-step verification. If credentials leaked, an attacker has full company control.
technical_explanation: Identity 'dev.admin@acmeretail.example' has AdministratorAccess IAM role, last login 142 days ago, and MFA is disabled.
potential_consequence: Silent administrative persistence and stealth data extraction.
recommended_action: Deactivate or delete the account and revoke all associated AWS IAM access keys.
remediation_steps: ["Deactivate dev.admin@acmeretail.example in Google Workspace Admin", "Delete AWS IAM user and access keys in AWS Console -> IAM", "Confirm contractor offboarding signoff"]

title: Administrator Account Missing MFA: Dev Ops Admin
business_impact: One or more administrator accounts do not have Multi-Factor Authentication enabled, making them susceptible to phishing.
technical_explanation: Account 'dev.admin@acmeretail.example' has administrative privileges but no TOTP or hardware FIDO2 factor configured.
potential_consequence: Single password compromise immediately yields root or admin level access.
remediation_steps: ["Enable 2-Step Verification enforcement in Google Workspace Admin Console", "Require security keys or Google Authenticator app"]

title: Unused Third-Party OAuth Integration Retains Data Write Access
business_impact: A marketing analytics bot hasn't been active in 3 months but still has permission to read user profiles and write files in your corporate workspace.
technical_explanation: Legacy Marketing Analytics Bot OAuth client has inactive_days=95 with scopes ['admin.directory.user.readonly', 'drive.file.write'].
potential_consequence: Supply chain compromise if the third-party analytics SaaS vendor suffers an intrusion.
recommended_action: Revoke OAuth client authorization in your Google Workspace Admin marketplace panel.
remediation_steps: ["Navigate to Security -> Access and data control -> API controls", "Locate Legacy Marketing Analytics Bot and click 'Block / Revoke Access'"]

title: Weak Email Security: DMARC Policy Set to 'none'
business_impact: Your email domain can be spoofed by attackers sending fake customer invoices or impersonating executives to your suppliers.
technical_explanation: DNS TXT record _dmarc.acmeretail.example specifies 'p=none' without rejection or quarantine enforcement.
potential_consequence: CEO fraud, fake invoice phishing, and email spoofing under your brand.
recommended_action: Upgrade DMARC policy from 'p=none' to 'p=quarantine' or 'p=reject'.
remediation_steps: ["Open DNS management in Cloudflare", "Update TXT record for _dmarc to 'v=DMARC1; p=reject; sp=reject; aspf=r;'", "Check DMARC reports inbox"]

title: Vulnerable Dependency in Application: lodash@4.17.20
business_impact: Your application depends on an insecure component (lodash@4.17.20). An attacker could exploit this known flaw to disrupt your online store or access internal services.
technical_explanation: lodash@4.17.20 is vulnerable to CVE-2021-23337 (CVSS 7.5, CWE-78). Prototype pollution in lodash leads to remote code execution or denial of service.
potential_consequence: Remote code execution, prototype pollution, or denial of service.
recommended_action: Upgrade package lodash@4.17.20 to version 4.17.21 or higher.
remediation_steps: ["Update package.json / requirements.txt to 4.17.21", "Run test suite to verify no breaking API changes", "Redeploy application and generate fresh SBOM"]

title: Extensive Blast Radius: Compromise of ecommerce-api Reaches Sensitive Data
business_impact: A security breach in 'ecommerce-api' would directly expose your critical business data (payment-service, Production PostgreSQL (Port 5432), acme-product-images, Customer PII & Order Records, acme-database-backups). An attacker could steal sensitive customer records, financial transactions, or credentials.
technical_explanation: Asset 'ecommerce-api' (Application) maintains direct or transitive network/authorization relationships to high-value data nodes (payment-service, Production PostgreSQL (Port 5432), acme-product-images, Customer PII & Order Records, acme-database-backups) across 14 graph hops.
potential_consequence: Mass customer data leak, regulatory penalties (GDPR/PCI-DSS), and reputational loss.
recommended_action: Enforce strict network segmentation and least-privilege IAM policies between ecommerce-api and payment-service, Production PostgreSQL (Port 5432), acme-product-images, Customer PII & Order Records, acme-database-backups.
remediation_steps: ["Isolate ecommerce-api into a private VPC or restrict ingress firewall rules", "Revoke direct access permissions to payment-service, Production PostgreSQL (Port 5432), acme-product-images, Customer PII & Order Records, acme-database-backups", "Implement application-level tokenization or field encryption"]

title: Viable Attack Path: Production PostgreSQL (Port 5432) → acme-database-backups
business_impact: A viable attack chain exists from the public Internet (Production PostgreSQL (Port 5432)) directly into 'acme-database-backups'. An external bad actor could compromise intermediate components to compromise your customer data.
technical_explanation: Graph traversal detected an unblocked 2-hop path: Production PostgreSQL (Port 5432) -> acme-database-backups. Choke point identified at 'intermediate gateway'.
potential_consequence: Complete compromise of backend data stores from an external unauthenticated entrypoint.
recommended_action: Sever the attack path by implementing an access barrier at choke point: 'intermediate gateway'.
remediation_steps: ["Place choke point 'intermediate gateway' behind an internal security group", "Disable direct ingress routing from Production PostgreSQL (Port 5432)", "Validate that ingress path is blocked in Digital Twin simulator"]
